newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH says Guinness buyback positive.
newsitem.headline: LVMH says Guinness buyback positive.

text.p: LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault said on Thursday that the group would finance the proposed purchase of Guinness Plc's stakes in their joint distribution ventures and Moet Hennessy with debt and that the move would have a positive impact on LVMH's results.

Asked at the shareholders' meeting how LVMH proposed to finance the purchase of Guinness's stake in the ventures and its 34 percent participation in Moet Hennessy, Arnaud said LVMH would finance the deal with debt.
He said such a transaction would not be incompatible with its balance sheet.
"This debt would have a postive impact on LVMH's accounts," he told shareholders.
A spokeswoman said the impact on the results would be positive because LVMH would be entitled to buy the participations back at a discount under prior accords between the two companies.

LVMH said on Wednesday that, as a result of the proposed merger between Grand Metropolitan and Guinness, it had the right to exercise options to buy the Guinness participations in the distriubution ventures and Moet Hennessy.

"The merger plan will have as a consequence a change in the Guinness ownership, bringing in a competitor," he said. "We thus decided if the plan goes ahead, to exercise (the) options," he said. He reiterated his opposition to the merger.

He also ruled out any plan by LVMH to sell its drinks businesses. "The wines and spirits at the heart of Moet Hennessy are a fundamental part of LVMH's strategy and a disposal is ruled out completely," he said.
LVMH's proposal is to bring together in one group the wines and spirits businesses of LVMH, Grand Met and Guinness.
The merger of Guinness and Grand Met would create a food and drinks group worth more than 20 billion pounds.
